samples.summary: Non-envelope backend error bodies now lose their `message` entirely — Nest's detailed 400/403/404 messages are replaced by a bare `HTTP <status>`
samples.evidence: `isErrorEnvelope` only accepts `{error:{code:string}}`. The backend produces that shape for exactly one case (`TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY`, packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42). Every other failure is a stock Nest exception — e.g. `throw new BadRequestException("Invalid block at ${path}: 'id' must be a non-empty string")` (docs-content.controller.ts:260), `NotFoundException('Document has no file')` (files.controller.ts:141), `ForbiddenException('This API key does not have write access')` (files.controller.ts:81) — which serialize to `{message, error:'Bad Request', statusCode}`. Before this change those bodies were printed verbatim, so the operator saw *which* block was invalid or *why* access was denied. Now `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 400'}}` and `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP 400` into `outputError`, discarding the only diagnostic the server sent. Rejecting the mis-shaped envelope is right; dropping the `message` string with it is a real regression in error reporting on the most common failure paths (validation, auth, not-found) across docs/notes/slides import, files upload/download and all six content/export commands. Folding a string `body.message` (or `body.error` when it is a string) into the synthesized envelope's `message` would preserve it.

samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson` is used on a success response with missing bytes, emitting a nonsensical `HTTP 200` error message
samples.evidence: The guard is `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`. When the download succeeded (`ok:true`, `status:200`) but `bytes` is absent, `upstreamErrorJson(res)` falls to its non-envelope branch and prints `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP 200'}}` — a 200 reported as an HTTP error, with no indication the real problem was an empty body. Previously the message field did not exist, so nothing contradicted itself. A distinct code/message for the bytes-missing case would be clearer.

samples.summary: Newly required font weights are not weights the app ever requests, risking a 10s `waitForFunction` timeout that fails the visual lane
samples.evidence: `VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS = [400,500,600,700]` is now required for every family. But index.html:12 requests Fraunces only at 500;600;700 (no 400) and JetBrains Mono only at 400;500 (no 600/700), and the lazily-injected families use `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS = '400;700'` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-catalog.ts:94). `document.fonts.check` normally satisfies these via CSS nearest-weight matching, so this may be benign — but any case where the matched face is in `error`/unloaded status makes the `waitForFunction` at line 386 never settle and abort the capture after 10s. Requiring only the weights actually served per family would remove the risk.

samples.summary: Swallowing `document.fonts.load` rejections can make the font guard pass silently when the Google Fonts stylesheet itself fails to load
samples.evidence: `document.fonts.load(...).catch(() => {})` discards the fetch failure. The comment claims the later `check` pass turns that into a named timeout, but that only holds when the face is registered and errored. If the stylesheet request fails (offline/blocked CI), no FontFace is ever registered for Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, `document.fonts.check` returns true by falling back to a system font, and the new catch-all `[...document.fonts]` poll sees no loading faces — so the guard passes and the screenshots are captured in the fallback serif, exactly the drift the change is meant to prevent. Asserting the family is actually registered (e.g. non-empty match in `document.fonts`) would close the hole.

verdict.reason: Verified all three legs independently. (1) formatter.ts:76-85 `isErrorEnvelope` accepts only `{error:{code:string}}`; `upstreamErrorJson` (:123-133) discards `res.data` and returns `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR',message:'HTTP <status>'}}`, and `forwardUpstreamError` (:100-110) throws `HTTP <status>` into `outputError` (:57-63) — neither folds in a string `body.message`. (2) No global Nest exception filter exists (grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters|@Catch` in packages/backend/src returned no matches), so ordinary throws serialize to `{message, error, statusCode}`; the cited throws are real (docs-content.controller.ts:260, files.controller.ts:81 and :141, plus tabs/images/documents/workspace-scope), while only docs-content.controller.ts:42 TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY has envelope shape. (3) http-client.ts:184-185/265/369-370 place the parsed body (with `message`) into `res.data`, and the task doc lines 38-40 confirm these sites previously printed `res.data` verbatim — so the server's only diagnostic is now dropped on the most common failure paths. I weighed refuting as out-of-scope since the task doc's acceptance criteria (lines 44-47) make the `HTTP <status>` output intentional and the failure is still signalled with exit code 1, but the Correctness lens explicitly covers error handling that swallows failures, and rejecting the mis-shaped `error` field does not require discarding a sibling string `message`. No guard elsewhere restores it.
